Surah 64 (al-Taghabun): Makkan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} These noble verses comprise a great and wide range of the glorious attributes of the Creator. He mentions the perfection of His divinity, glorified and exalted is He, the vastness of His self-sufficiency, and the dependence of all creation upon Him; the glorification of whoever is in the heavens and the earth with the praise of their Lord; and that all dominion belongs to Allah, so no creature falls outside His dominion. All praise belongs entirely to Him: praise for the attributes of perfection He possesses, praise for the things He brought into existence, praise for the laws He prescribed, and praise for the blessings He bestowed. His power is all-encompassing, and no existing thing falls outside it, so nothing that He wills is beyond His ability to accomplish.

{2} He mentions that He created the servants and made among them the believer and the disbeliever. Their faith and their disbelief are entirely by the decree and predestination of Allah, and it is He who willed that for them, by giving them capacity and will through which they are able to do whatever they wish of obedience and disobedience. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

{3} When He mentioned the creation of man, the one commanded and forbidden, He mentioned the creation of the rest of the creatures, saying: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, their bodies and all that is in them, and He perfected their creation. ﴿In truth﴾; that is, with wisdom and the purpose intended by the Exalted. ﴿And He shaped you and perfected your forms﴾; as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾. So man is the best of creatures in form and the most splendid in appearance. ﴿And to Him is the final destination﴾; that is, the return on the Day of Resurrection, when He will recompense you for your faith and your disbelief, and will ask you about the blessings and bounties He bestowed upon you: did you give thanks for them, or did you not?

{4} Then He mentioned the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, saying: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, the hidden and the apparent, the unseen and the witnessed. ﴿And He knows what you conceal and what you declare, and Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts﴾; that is, of what they contain of good secrets, hidden evils, righteous intentions, and corrupt aims. If He is Knowing of what is within the breasts, then it is incumbent upon the intelligent and perceptive person to strive and exert effort to guard his inner self from blameworthy character traits and to adorn himself with beautiful character.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 64, verses 5–6:

{5} When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned His perfect and great attributes, by which He is known, worshipped, and by which effort is exerted to win His good pleasure and His displeasure is avoided, He informed of what He did to the earlier nations and the past generations, whose reports continue to be narrated by later generations and related by the truthful. When their messengers came to them with the truth, they denied them and opposed them, so Allah made them taste the evil consequence of their affair in this world and disgraced them in it. {And for them is a painful punishment}: in the Hereafter.

{6} For this reason He mentioned the cause of this punishment, saying: {That}: the chastisement and evil consequence which We inflicted upon them, {because there came to them their messengers with clear proofs}; that is, with clear signs indicating the truth and falsehood. So they recoiled and became arrogant towards their messengers, and said: {Shall mere mortals guide us?}; that is, they have no superiority over us; and why did Allah choose them over us? As He said in another verse: {Their messengers said to them, "We are only mortals like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants."} So they denied the favour and grace of Allah upon His prophets, that they should be messengers to creation, and they were arrogant against submitting to them, so they were afflicted with worshipping trees, stones, and the like. {So they disbelieved} in Allah, {and turned away} from His obedience, {and Allah was self-sufficient} regarding them; He does not care for them, and their misguidance does not harm Him at all. {And Allah is Rich, Praiseworthy}; that is, He is the Self-Sufficient who possesses complete and absolute sufficiency from all aspects, the Praiseworthy in His sayings, His actions, and His attributes.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 64, verses 5–6:

{7} He, may He be exalted, informs of the obstinacy of the disbelievers, their false claim, and their denial of the Resurrection, without knowledge, without guidance, and without an illuminating Book. So He commanded the noblest of His creation to swear by his Lord regarding their being resurrected and recompensed for their wicked deeds and their denial of the truth. {And that is easy for Allah}: for although it is difficult, or rather impossible, in relation to creation, since if all their powers combined to bring a single dead person back to life, they would not be able to do so, yet as for Allah, may He be exalted, when He wills something, He says to it: "Be," and it is. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and thereupon they will be standing, looking on.﴾

{8} When Allah mentioned the denial of those who denied the Resurrection, and that this denial of theirs necessitates their disbelief in Allah and His signs, He commanded what protects from destruction and misery, namely faith in Him, in His Messenger, and in His Book. Allah named it "light" (nur), because light is the opposite of darkness. Thus, what is in the Book that Allah sent down of rulings, laws and reports are lights by which one is guided through the thick darkness of ignorance, and by which one walks in the pitch-black gloom of the night. Whatever is other than being guided by the Book of Allah consists of sciences whose harm exceeds their benefit and whose evil exceeds their good; rather, there is no good or benefit in them, except what agrees with what the Messengers brought. Faith in Allah, His Messenger, and His Book requires complete certainty and true conviction in them, and acting in accordance with that belief by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. {And Allah is Acquainted with what you do}: He will recompense you for your good and evil deeds.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 64, verses 9–10:

{9} That is: remember the Day of Assembly (yawm al-jam'), the Day on which Allah will gather the first and the last, will make them stand in a terrifying and tremendous station, and will inform them of what they did. Then the difference (al-farq) and the mutual loss and gain (al-taghabun) among creatures will become manifest. Some folk will be raised to 'Illiyyun (ʿIlliyyūn), into the lofty chambers and elevated dwellings that comprise every pleasure and desire, and some folk will be lowered to the lowest of the low (asfal safilin), the place of distress, grief, sorrow and severe punishment. This is the outcome of what they sent forward for themselves and advanced during the days of their lives. Therefore He said: ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾; that is, the difference and disparity among creatures will become manifest on it, the believers will defraud the wicked, and the criminals will know that they were upon nothing, and that they are the losers. It is as if it were said: by what does success, wretchedness, bliss and punishment come about? So He mentioned the causes of that in His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾: with complete faith that encompasses everything Allah commanded belief in, ﴿and does righteousness﴾: from the obligatory and the voluntary acts, including discharging the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants, ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: in them is what the souls desire, what the eyes find delight in, what the spirits choose, what the hearts yearn for, and it will be the culmination of every desired thing. ﴿Abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

{10} ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾; that is, they disbelieved in them without any legal or rational basis, rather the proofs and clear evidences came to them, yet they denied them and opposed what they indicated. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever, and wretched is the destination.﴾ Because it gathers every misery, hardship, wretchedness and punishment.

{10} ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs﴾; that is, they disbelieved in them without any legal or rational basis, rather the proofs and clear evidences came to them, yet they denied them and opposed what they indicated. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever, and wretched is the destination.﴾ Because it gathers every misery, hardship, wretchedness and punishment.

{11} He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿No disaster strikes except by the permission of Allah﴾. This is general to all calamities, whether to the self, wealth, children, loved ones and the like. Everything that befalls the servants is by the decree and destiny of Allah. Allah's knowledge has already encompassed this, His pen has written it, His will has taken effect, and His wisdom has required it. But the matter of utmost importance is this: will the servant perform the duty incumbent upon him in this situation or not? If he performs it, then he will have abundant reward and a beautiful recompense in this world and the Hereafter. When he believes that it is from Allah, is content with it, and submits to His command, Allah guides his heart, so he is at peace and is not agitated at calamities, unlike those whom Allah has not guided. Rather, Allah grants him steadfastness when they come and the fulfilment of what patience requires. Thus he obtains an immediate reward, along with the great recompense that Allah stores up for him on the Day of Recompense, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without reckoning﴾.

It is known from this that whoever does not believe in Allah when calamities come, in that he does not consider the decree and destiny of Allah but stops only at the mere means, will be forsaken, and Allah will leave him to himself. When a servant is left to himself, the self has nothing but anxiety and distress, which is an immediate punishment upon the servant before the punishment of the Hereafter, for having neglected the obligation of patience. This is what relates to His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾ in the specific context of calamities. As for what relates to it in terms of general wording, Allah informed that every one who believes – i.e., the faith commanded, which is belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, good and bad – and makes his faith true by what faith requires of its necessary implications and obligations, this means that the cause by which the servant acts is the greatest cause for Allah's guidance of him in his words, deeds, all his states, in his knowledge and his action. This is the best recompense Allah gives to the people of faith, as Allah, may He be exalted, said, informing that He makes the believers firm in this world and in the Hereafter, and the root of steadfastness is the firmness of the heart, its patience and its certainty at the arrival of every trial. He said: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. So the people of faith are the most guided of people in heart and the most steadfast at times of distress and anxiety, because of the faith they possess.

{12} And His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, i.e., in carrying out their commands and avoiding their prohibitions, for obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger is the axis of happiness and the sign of success. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., from obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, ﴿then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾, i.e., he conveys to you what he was sent with, a clear and evident conveyance, so the proof is established against you. He has no power over your guidance or your reckoning. He only holds you to account for carrying out obedience to Allah and His Messenger or failing to do so, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.

{13} ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him﴾, i.e., He is the one deserving worship and divinity; every object of worship other than Him is false. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, i.e., let them depend upon Him in every matter that confronts them and in what they intend to undertake, for no matter is made easy except by Allah, and there is no path to that except by relying upon Allah. Reliance upon Allah is not complete until the servant thinks well of his Lord and trusts Him to suffice him in the matter on which he relies. According to the servant's faith, his reliance is strong or weak.

This is a warning from God to the believers against being deceived by spouses and children, for some of them are an enemy to you. An enemy is one who wants evil for you, so your duty is to be wary of one who has this description. The soul is naturally disposed to love spouses and children, so God advised His servants that this love should lead them to comply with the demands of spouses and children only where those demands involve no legal harm. He encouraged them to obey His commands and to give precedence to His good pleasure, through the great reward He has with Him, which includes lofty aims and precious objects of love, and to prefer the Hereafter over the transient, fleeting world. Since the prohibition against obeying spouses and children in what harms the servant, and the warning against that, may give the impression of harshness toward them and of punishing them, God commanded that they be guarded against, and that one pardon them, overlook their faults, and forgive, for in that there are benefits that cannot be counted. So He said: ﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Whoever pardons, Allah pardons him; whoever overlooks, Allah overlooks [his faults]; and whoever deals with Allah [Most High] in what He loves, and deals with His servants in what they love and what benefits them, attains the love of Allah and the love of His servants, and his affairs are set in good order for him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 64, verses 16–18:

{16} He, exalted is He, commands taqwa (fear and awareness of God), which is complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and He restricts this by capacity and ability. This verse indicates that every obligation which the servant is unable to perform falls away from him, and that if he is able to do some of what is commanded and unable to do some of it, he performs what he is able to do and what he is unable to do falls away from him. This is as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If I command you with a matter, then do of it what you are able." Under this legal principle (qa'idah shar'iyyah) fall countless branches of the law. His words {and listen} mean: listen to what God admonishes you with and what He prescribes for you of rulings, know that, and submit to it. {And obey} means: obey God and His Messenger in all your affairs. {And spend} means: spend of the [lawful] expenditures, both obligatory and recommended; that act will be good for you in this world and the Hereafter, for all good lies in complying with the commands of God [exalted is He], accepting His counsel, and submitting to His law, and all evil lies in opposing that. However, there is a blight that prevents many people from spending as commanded, namely miserliness (shuhh), with which most souls are innately disposed; they are stingy with wealth, love its possession, and hate its leaving the hand to an extreme degree. Whoever God [exalted is He] protects from {the miserliness of his own soul}, by his soul being generous in spending that benefits it, {those are the successful}, because they have attained what is sought and been saved from what is feared. Indeed, this may encompass everything the servant is commanded or forbidden to do, for if his soul is miserly, not submitting to what it is commanded and not giving out what is due from it, he will not succeed, but will lose both this world and the Hereafter. And if his soul is generous, at peace, and expanded toward God's law, seeking His good pleasure, then between it and doing what it is charged with there is nothing but knowledge of it, the arrival of its knowledge to it, and insight that it pleases God [exalted is He]; by that it succeeds, prospers, and wins every kind of success.

{17} Then He, exalted is He, encouraged spending, saying: {If you lend to God a goodly loan}, which is every expenditure made from lawful means when the servant intends by it the face of God, exalted is He, and places it in its proper place. {He will multiply it for you}: the expenditure, tenfold up to seven hundred times, and to many multiples beyond that. Along with the multiplication, {and He will forgive you}, by reason of spending and charity, your sins; for God erases sins through charities and good deeds, {indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds}. {God is Most Appreciative, Forbearing}: He does not hasten to punish the one who disobeys Him, but gives him respite without neglecting him. {If God were to take mankind to task for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back a single creature, but He defers them to a specified term} (Qur'an 35:45). God, exalted is He, is Most Appreciative: He accepts from His servants little deeds and rewards them with much reward, and He appreciates those who bear hardships and burdens for His sake and various heavy obligations, and whoever leaves something for God, God replaces it for him with something better.

{18} {Knower of the unseen and the witnessed}: that is, what is hidden from the servants of the hosts that no one knows but Him, and what they witness of creation. {The Almighty}: the One who cannot be overcome or prevented, who has subdued all things. {The Wise}: in His creation and His command, who places things in their proper places.

The commentary of the surah is complete. And to God belongs all praise.
